items.q: What filter did Leclerc keep after Formula 1 year one?
items.a: Only **people he loves most**. Karting and F2 mistakes were mum-and-dad scale. Year one he **read everything**. Driving errors stay **part of the sport**.

items.q: Which critics hurt more than a bad lap?
items.a: **Identity-wrong reads** — "look how arrogant he is" when he is not. Show the **true self** on social, then accept you will not be liked by everyone.

items.q: What changed about Leclerc being extremely harsh on himself?
items.a: The **honesty** stayed. The **reaction** changed. Junior version collapsed confidence. Adult version converts the mistake into learning and keeps direction.
The next one is in about **one second**. Adrenaline helps **in the car**. The long wound is **1–2 weeks** of post-race rumination.

items.q: When is he scared if not in the car?
items.a: Fear tracks **agency**. 0% scared when driving. Snakes, bungee, and watching **brother Arthur** race are different — every race is "a torture."

sections.title: Grief and the father's two words

items.q: What did he ask the Tuesday his father died in Baku 2017?
items.a: **What would he want me to do?** One answer: fly Wednesday and try to win. Extra motivation, not a performance of suffering.

items.q: What do humble and grateful actually do?
items.a: **Humble** is a work-rate rule — don't ease off after four good races. **Grateful** is the hard-stretch practice when Ferrari pressure and comments pile on.

items.q: What happens to Pierre Gasly when the visor closes?
items.a: He is **nobody**. Real friends off-track since 2005; **no advice, no gifts** on-track. F1 is a **team sport in the shadows** (~1,500 people in Maranello).

items.q: How far out were the goals from age five?
items.a: **One or two months**, always in the right direction — not a 10–15 year fantasy. Leave the track having learned something. Sleep 10–11 hours; **cold baths** bookend race day; piano is the disconnect.
